sentences.zh: 常思，字克恭，太原人也。

translations.literal: Chang Si, whose style name was Kejing, was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Si, style name Kejing, was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父仁嶽，河東牙將，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His father Ren Yue was a military aide of Hedong and was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren Yue had served as a military aide in Hedong and was repeatedly posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗之為晉王也，廣募勝兵，時思以趫悍應募，累從戎役，後為長直都校，歷捧聖軍使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong of Tang was Prince of Jin, he widely recruited elite troops; at that time Si joined the recruitment on account of his swift daring, followed campaigns repeatedly, later became commander of the Long Straight guard, and eventually served as commissioner of the Sacred Support Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong of Tang was still Prince of Jin, he raised troops far and wide; Si enlisted for his speed and boldness, saw action in campaign after campaign, and rose from commander of the Long Straight guard to commissioner of the Sacred Support Army.

sentences.zh: 晉初，遷六軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jin period, he was transferred to Grand Commandant of Inspectors for the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Tang, he was made Grand Commandant of Inspectors for the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖出鎮並門，奏以思從行，尋表為河東牢城都指揮使，以勤幹見稱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han went out to govern at Bingmen, he memorialized that Si should accompany him; soon he was memorialized as Grand Commandant directing the Hedong fortified-city garrison and became known for diligence and capability.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Gaozu of Han took up his post at Taiyuan, he had Si accompany him and soon had him appointed to command the Hedong fortified-city garrison, where his industry and efficiency won notice.

sentences.zh: 漢國初建，授檢校太保，遙領鄧州。

translations.literal: When the Han state was first established, he was appointed Acting Grand Guardian and held Deng Prefecture in title only.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Later Han, he received the acting rank of Grand Guardian and a nominal commission over Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，遷檢校太尉、昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the Han held the realm, he was transferred to Acting Grand Commandant and military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Han ruled the empire, he was promoted to Acting Grand Commandant and made military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 乾佑初，李守貞叛於河中，太祖征之，朝廷命思帥部兵以副焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyou reign, Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong; the Taizu campaigned against him, and the court ordered Si to lead his troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyou era, when Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, Taizu marched against him and the court ordered Si to bring his forces as a subordinate column.

sentences.zh: 既而禦眾無能，勒歸舊藩。

translations.literal: Before long, because he proved incapable of commanding troops, he was compelled to return to his former fief.
translations.idiomatic: He soon proved unable to handle his troops and was ordered back to his old command.

sentences.zh: 思在上黨凡五年，無令譽可稱，唯以聚斂為務，性又鄙吝，未嘗與賓佐有酒肴之會。

translations.literal: Si spent five years altogether at Shangdang with no reputation worth mentioning; he devoted himself solely to exactions, and by nature he was mean and stingy, never once hosting his staff with food and wine.
translations.idiomatic: For five years at Shangdang, Si earned no good name: he cared only for squeezing revenue, was tight-fisted by nature, and never once treated his staff to a meal or a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 嘗有從事欲求謁見者，思覽刺而怒曰：「彼必是來獵酒也。

translations.literal: Once a staff member sought an audience; Si read his calling card and said angrily, "He must be coming to hunt for wine."
translations.idiomatic: When a staff officer once asked for an audience, Si read his card and snapped, "He only wants to wheedle wine out of me."

sentences.zh: 」命典客者飲而遣之，其鄙吝也如是。

translations.literal: He ordered the reception officer to give him drink and send him away; such was his stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: He had the usher give the man a drink and show him out—such was his meanness.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，就加平章事。

translations.literal: When the Taizu received the Mandate, Si was at once made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Si was immediately made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖微時，以季父待思，及即位，遣其妻入覲，太祖拜之如家人之禮，仍呼曰叔母，其恩顧如是。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Taizu was still obscure, he treated Si as a younger uncle; after his accession he sent Si's wife to court for an audience, and the Taizu bowed to her with the rites due within the family, still calling her aunt; such was his favor toward them.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Taizu had treated Si like a younger uncle; after he became emperor he summoned Si's wife to court and greeted her with the deference one shows kin, still calling her "Aunt"—so deep was his regard.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年秋，思來朝，加兼侍中，移鎮宋州。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Guangshun, Si came to court, was additionally made Vice Grand Secretary, and was transferred to garrison Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Guangshun 2, Si came to court, was made Vice Grand Secretary as well, and was reassigned to Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，詔赴闕，改授平盧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year he was ordered to the capital and reassigned as military commissioner of the Pinglu Army.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer he was summoned to court and made military commissioner of the Pinglu Army.

sentences.zh: 思將赴鎮，奏太祖云：「臣在宋州出鎮，得絲十餘萬兩，謹以上進，請行征督。

translations.literal: As Si was about to depart for his new post, he memorialized the Taizu, saying, "When I left my post at Song Prefecture I had more than a hundred thousand taels of silk, which I respectfully present; I ask permission to pursue collection."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving for his new command, Si reported to Taizu: "When I left Song Prefecture I had over a hundred thousand taels of silk, which I now offer up; please let me continue to collect what is owed."

sentences.zh: 」太祖頷之，尋詔本州折券以諭其民。

translations.literal: The Taizu nodded assent, and soon an edict was issued in that prefecture to cancel the bonds and inform the people.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu nodded, and soon ordered the bonds in that prefecture torn up and the people told.

sentences.zh: 及到鎮，未幾，染風痹之疾，上表請尋醫，既而舁疾歸洛。

translations.literal: After he reached his post, before long he contracted a wind-paralysis ailment, memorialized to seek medical treatment, and was soon carried home ill to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took up his post he fell ill with wind paralysis, asked leave to seek treatment, and was carried back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年春卒，年六十有九。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of Xiande 1, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Chief Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Chief Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 翟光鄴，字化基，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: Zhai Guangye, whose style name was Huaji, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Guangye, style name Huaji, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 父景珂，倜儻有膽氣。

translations.literal: His father Jing Ke was free-spirited and full of courage.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing Ke was bold and high-spirited.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明初，唐莊宗始駐軍於河上，景珂率聚邑人守永定驛，固守逾年，後為北軍所攻，景珂戰歿，眾潰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenming reign of Liang, Zhuangzong of Tang first stationed troops on the Yellow River; Jing Ke led the people of his district to hold Yongding Post, defending stubbornly for more than a year until the northern army attacked, Jing Ke died in battle, and the host scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang's Zhenming era, when Zhuangzong of Tang first camped on the Yellow River, Jing Ke rallied his neighbors to hold Yongding Post for over a year until the northern army broke in; Jing Ke fell in battle and his men fled.

sentences.zh: 光鄴時年十歲，為明宗軍所俘，以其穎悟，俾侍左右，字之曰永定。

translations.literal: Guangye was then ten years old; he was captured by Mingzong's army, and because he was quick-witted he was made to attend at his side and given the style name Yongding.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye was only ten when Mingzong's troops captured him; struck by the boy's quick mind, the emperor kept him at his side and gave him the style name Yongding.

sentences.zh: 既冠，沈毅有謀，蒞事寡過。

translations.literal: After he came of age he was grave, resolute, and resourceful, and in handling affairs seldom erred.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came of age he proved steady, shrewd, and seldom at fault in office.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，時深委遇，累遷至皇城使、檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he at that time entrusted Guangye deeply and promoted him repeatedly until he reached Imperial City Commissioner and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he won deep trust and rose through the ranks to Imperial City Commissioner and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 長興中，樞密使安重誨得罪，時光鄴與中官孟小僧頗有力焉。

translations.literal: During the Changxing era, when Chief Councillor An Chonghui fell from favor, Guangye and the eunuch Meng Xiaoseng were quite influential in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, when Chief Councillor An Chonghui fell, Guangye and the eunuch Meng Xiaoseng had played no small part.

sentences.zh: 居無何，出為耀州團練使。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as regimental commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was posted out as regimental commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，入為左監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he entered service as Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai he returned to court as Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，歷棣沂二州刺史、西京副留守。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era of Jin he served in succession as prefect of Di and Yi Prefectures and as deputy defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Jin's Tianfu reign he served as prefect of Di and Yi in turn and as deputy defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 開運初，授宣徽使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was appointed Palace Secretariat Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaiyun he was made Palace Secretariat Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠叛滅，青州平，除為防禦使，朝廷以兵亂之後，人物雕弊，故命光鄴理之。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan's rebellion was destroyed and Qingzhou pacified, Guangye was made defense commissioner; because after the military turmoil the population was devastated, the court ordered Guangye to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Guangyuan's rebellion was crushed and Qingzhou pacified, he was made defense commissioner; with the region laid waste by war, the court sent Guangye to rebuild it.

sentences.zh: 光鄴好聚書，重儒者，虛齋論議，惟求理道。

translations.literal: Guangye loved to collect books, honored Confucian scholars, and in his empty study held discussions seeking only the principles of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He collected books, honored scholars, and in his spare study debated nothing but principle and right conduct.

sentences.zh: 時郡民喪亡十之六七，而招懷撫諭，視之如傷，故期月之間，流亡載輯。

translations.literal: At that time six or seven tenths of the prefecture's people had perished, yet he recruited, comforted, and instructed them, treating their wounds as his own, so that within a month the exiles were largely gathered back.
translations.idiomatic: Six or seven in ten of the people had died, yet he drew in the survivors with gentle care, and within a month the exiles were streaming home.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，偽命權知曹州。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, a false order made him acting prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans took Bian, they installed him as acting prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 李從益假號，以光鄴明宗舊臣，署為樞密使。

translations.literal: When Li Congyi assumed a false title, because Guangye was an old minister of Mingzong, he was appointed Chief Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Congyi claimed the throne, he named Guangye Chief Councillor as a former servant of Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 漢祖至汴，改左領衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Han founder reached Bian, Guangye was changed to Grand General of the Left Leading Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Han reached Bian, he was made Grand General of the Left Leading Guard.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，遷右金吾衛大將軍，充街使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, served as street commissioner, and was made Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he became Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard, street commissioner, and Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，復授宣徽使、左千牛衛上將軍、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, Guangye was again made Palace Secretariat Commissioner, Senior General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard, and Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, he again received the posts of Palace Secretariat Commissioner, Senior General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard, and Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 數月，兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: Several months later he additionally served as Deputy Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was also made Deputy Chief Councillor.

sentences.zh: 會永興李洪信入朝，代知軍府事。

translations.literal: When Li Hongxin of Yongxing came to court, Guangye acted in his stead to manage the military administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongxin of Yongxing came to court, he took over the military administration in his stead.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年十月，卒於長安，時年四十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Guangshun he died at Chang'an, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Chang'an in the tenth month of Guangshun 2, aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 光鄴有器度，慎密敦厚，出於天然，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Guangye had breadth of character, was cautious, discreet, and sincere by nature, and never let pleasure or anger show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He had true breadth of mind—cautious, discreet, and naturally kind—and never let pleasure or anger show.

sentences.zh: 事繼母以孝聞，兄弟皆雍睦。

translations.literal: He was known for filial devotion to his stepmother, and his brothers all lived in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: His filial care for his stepmother was renowned, and he lived in harmony with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 雖食祿日久，家無餘財，任金吾日，假官屋數間以蔽風雨，親族累重，糲食才給，人不堪其憂，光鄴處之晏如也。

translations.literal: Although he had drawn salary for a long time, his household had no surplus wealth; while serving as Golden Crow commissioner he borrowed a few government rooms to shelter from wind and rain, his kin were numerous, and coarse food barely sufficed—others could not bear such hardship, yet Guangye dwelt in perfect ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had drawn salary for years, his house held no spare cash; as Golden Crow commissioner he rented a few government rooms against the weather, and with a large clan to feed on coarse grain alone others would have despaired—yet he remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 賓朋至，則貰酒延之，談說終日，略無厭倦，士大夫多之。

translations.literal: When guests arrived he would buy wine to entertain them and talk all day without the least weariness; the scholar-official class greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: When friends came he bought wine on credit and talked the day away without tiring; men of letters held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及權知京兆，以寬靜為治，前政有煩苛之事，一切停罷，百姓便之。

translations.literal: When he acted as administrator of the Capital District, he governed with leniency and calm; whatever troublesome or harsh measures the previous administration had imposed, he halted them all, to the people's benefit.
translations.idiomatic: As acting administrator of the Capital District he ruled with leniency and calm, abolishing every harsh practice of his predecessors to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 及病甚，召親隨於臥內，戒之曰：「氣絕之後，以屍歸洛，不得於此停留，慮煩軍府。

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe he summoned his close attendants to his bedside and admonished them, saying, "After my breath is cut off, take my body back to Luoyang; do not let it remain here, lest it trouble the military administration."
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he called his attendants to his bedside and said, "When I am gone, take my body back to Luoyang—do not leave it here and burden the command."

sentences.zh: 」言訖而終。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died as soon as he had spoken.

sentences.zh: 京兆吏如喪所親，或有以漿酒遙奠者。

translations.literal: The officials of the Capital District mourned as if they had lost kin, and some poured libations of gruel and wine from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital District staff mourned him like a kinsman; some even poured libations from a distance.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王峻素重光鄴，且欲厚恤其家，為之上請，故自終及葬，所賜賻赗幾數千計。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Wang Jun had always held Guangye in high regard and wished to provide generously for his family; he memorialized on their behalf, so that from death through burial the gifts of condolence and burial goods amounted to nearly a thousand items.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Wang Jun, who had long esteemed him, petitioned for a generous settlement of his family, so that from death to burial the court's gifts ran to nearly a thousand items.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太子少師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 光鄴膚革肥皙，善於攝養，故司天監趙延乂有袁、許之術，嘗謂人曰：「翟君外厚而內薄，雖貴而無壽。

translations.literal: Guangye's skin was plump and fair and he was skilled at nurturing his health; therefore Zhao Yanyi of the Directorate of Astronomy, who possessed the arts of Yuan and Xu, once told others, "Master Zhai is outwardly full but inwardly thin; though honored, he will not live long."
translations.idiomatic: Guangye's complexion was plump and fair and he took good care of himself; Zhao Yanyi of the Directorate of Astronomy, versed in physiognomy in the manner of Yuan and Xu, once said, "Master Zhai looks robust but is hollow within—rank will not buy him long life."

sentences.zh: 」果如其言。

translations.literal: It turned out exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 曹英，字德秀，舊名犯今上御名，故改焉。

translations.literal: Cao Ying, whose style name was Dexiu, had an original name that violated the present emperor's taboo name and was therefore changed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ying, style name Dexiu, had been given a birth name that tabooed the reigning emperor's name and was renamed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 本常山鎮定人也。

translations.literal: He was originally a native of Zhending in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally from Zhending in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 父全武，事趙王王镕為列校，英因得隸於镕之帳下。

translations.literal: His father Quanwu served King Wang Rong of Zhao as a company commander, and Ying thereby came to serve under Rong's command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quanwu had served Zhao's King Wang Rong as a company commander, and Ying entered Rong's service through that connection.

sentences.zh: 及張文禮之亂，唐莊宗奄有其地，乃錄镕之左右，署為散指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhang Wenli's rebellion occurred, Zhuangzong of Tang suddenly seized the region, enrolled Rong's former attendants, and appointed Ying a roving commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wenli rebelled and Zhuangzong of Tang seized the region, he enrolled Rong's former followers and made Ying a roving commander.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，英侍於仗下，問其祖考，英以實對，明宗曰：「乃朕之舊也。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Ying attended below the imperial halberds; the emperor asked about his forebears, and Ying answered truthfully; Mingzong said, "He is an old acquaintance of mine."
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne, Ying stood guard at court; asked about his family, he answered frankly, and Mingzong said, "Why, he is an old friend of mine."

sentences.zh: 」擢為本班行首，每加顧遇。

translations.literal: He was promoted to head of his guard unit and received special favor on every occasion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made head of his guard unit and shown favor again and again.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，遷弩手軍使。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era of Jin he was transferred to commissioner of the Crossbowmen Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Jin's Tianfu reign he was made commissioner of the Crossbowmen Army.

sentences.zh: 平張從賓於汜水，以功授本軍都校。

translations.literal: When Zhang Congbin was pacified at Sishui, for his merit he was made commander of his army.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in crushing Zhang Congbin at Sishui he was made commander of his army.

sentences.zh: 漢初，改奉國軍主，加檢校司徒，兼康州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was changed to commander of the Supporting-the-State Army, made Acting Minister of Education, and concurrently prefect of Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han he was made commander of the Supporting-the-State Army, Acting Minister of Education, and concurrent prefect of Kang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，李守貞據河中叛，授行營步軍都校。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, when Li Shouzhen held Hezhong in rebellion, Ying was appointed commander of the campaign infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou, when Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, he was made commander of the campaign infantry.

sentences.zh: 河中平，遷本軍廂主，領岳州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, he was transferred to chief of his army's wing and made defense commissioner of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Hezhong fell he became chief of his army's wing and defense commissioner of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隨太祖在魏，為北面行營步軍都校，從平內難。

translations.literal: He followed the Taizu at Wei, served as commander of the northern campaign infantry, and took part in pacifying the internal crisis.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu at Wei as commander of the northern campaign infantry and helped put down the internal crisis.

sentences.zh: 國初，以翊戴功授昭武節度使、檢校太傅、侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, for his merit in supporting the enthronement he was made military commissioner of the Zhaowu Army, Acting Grand Mentor, and Grand Commandant directing the Palace Guard infantry.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he was rewarded for helping place Taizu on the throne with the Zhaowu commission, Acting Grand Mentor, and command of the Palace Guard infantry.

sentences.zh: 二年春，總兵討慕容彥超於兗州，梯沖塹壘，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he commanded troops against Murong Yanchao at Yan Prefecture and contributed greatly with scaling ladders, rams, trenches, and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he led the campaign against Murong Yanchao at Yanzhou, where his siege works did much to decide the day.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，太祖親征，因並兵攻陷其城，及凱旋，領彰信軍節度使，典軍如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer the Taizu campaigned in person; joining forces they stormed and took the city, and upon the triumphal return Ying was made military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army while retaining command of the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Taizu marched in person; their combined assault took the city, and on the triumphal return Ying was made military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army while keeping his army command.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，加同平章事，授成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Ying was made Associate Grand Councilor and military commissioner of the Chengde Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded him, Ying was made Associate Grand Councilor and military commissioner of the Chengde Army.

sentences.zh: 車駕自太原回，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned from Taiyuan, he was additionally made Vice Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Taiyuan, he was also made Vice Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年冬，卒於鎮，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xiande he died at his post, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post in the winter of Xiande 1, aged forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 制贈中書令。

translations.literal: By imperial order he was posthumously made Chief Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored him as Chief Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 英性沈厚，謙恭有禮，雖衽席之際，接對賓客，亦未嘗造次。

translations.literal: Ying's nature was deep and steady, humble and courteous; even in private at the sleeping mat, when receiving guests he never acted rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was grave and steady, humble and courteous; even in private he never treated guests with careless haste.

sentences.zh: 及卒，搢紳之士亦皆惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, the gentry and officials all lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death men of rank across the court mourned him.

sentences.zh: 李彥頵，字德循，太原人也。

translations.literal: Li Yanyun, whose style name was Dexun, was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanyun, style name Dexun, was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 本以商賈為業，太祖鎮鄴，置之左右，及即位，歷綾錦副使、搉易使。

translations.literal: He had originally made his living as a merchant; when the Taizu governed at Ye he placed Yanyun at his side, and after his accession Yanyun served in succession as deputy commissioner of brocades and as monopoly commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a merchant; when Taizu governed Ye he kept him close, and after the enthronement Yanyun rose through posts as deputy brocade commissioner and monopoly commissioner.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，以彥頵有舊，超授內客省使。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, because Yanyun was an old associate he was promoted out of turn to commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, remembering their old tie, skipped the usual steps and made him commissioner of the Inner Guests Bureau.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知相州軍府事，尋改延州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Before long he was made administrator of the Xiang Prefecture military government, and soon afterward was changed to military regent of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was administering Xiang Prefecture, then was posted as military regent of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 到鎮，頗以殖貨為意，窺圖剩利，侵漁蕃漢部人，群情大擾。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post he was much intent on amassing wealth, scheming for surplus profit and preying upon both tribal and Han subjects, so that public sentiment was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he set his mind on piling up wealth, squeezing every margin of profit from tribal and Han subjects alike until the whole region seethed.

sentences.zh: 會世宗南征，蕃部結聚，圍迫州城，彥頵閉壁自守，求援於鄰道，賴救兵至，乃解。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned south, tribal groups gathered and pressed the prefectural city; Yanyun shut the walls and held out, sought aid from neighboring circuits, and only when relief troops arrived was the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: During Shizong's southern campaign tribesmen gathered and besieged the city; Yanyun shut the gates and held out until neighboring circuits sent relief.

sentences.zh: 世宗不悅，征赴京師，然猶委曲庇護，竟不之責。

translations.literal: Shizong was displeased and summoned him to the capital, yet still sheltered him tactfully and in the end did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was displeased and recalled him to court, yet still shielded him and never held him to account.

sentences.zh: 尋為西京水南巡檢使，居無何，命權知泗州軍州事，改滄州兩使留後。

translations.literal: Soon he was made inspector south of the Western Capital's waterways; before long he was ordered to act as administrator of Sizhou's military and civil affairs, then was changed to regent of both civil and military affairs at Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made inspector south of the Western Capital's waterways, then acting administrator of Sizhou, and finally regent of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彥頵到任，處置乖方，大為物情所鄙。

translations.literal: When Yanyun took up his post his handling was perverse, and he was greatly despised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed at Cang he governed so badly that public opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 顯德六年秋，受代歸闕，遇疾而卒，時年五十有二。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Xiande he was relieved and returned to court, fell ill on the way, and died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Xiande 6 he was relieved and started back for court, but fell ill and died on the road at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 李暉，字順光，瀛州束城人。

translations.literal: Li Hui, whose style name was Shunguang, was a native of Dongcheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui, style name Shunguang, came from Dongcheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應募於龍驤軍，漢祖領河東，暉請從，因得署為河東牙將。

translations.literal: At his coming of age he enlisted in the Dragon Soaring Army; when the Han founder took command of Hedong, Hui asked to follow him and was thereby appointed a military aide of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he enlisted in the Dragon Soaring Army; when the founder of Han took Hedong, Hui asked to follow and was made a military aide there.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，授檢校司徒、大內皇城使。

translations.literal: When the Han held the realm, he was made Acting Minister of Education and commissioner of the Inner Imperial City.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Han ruled the empire he received the acting rank of Minister of Education and the post of Inner Imperial City commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to commissioner of the Southern Palace Secretariat Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commissioner of the Southern Palace Secretariat Court.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，拜河陽節度使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was appointed military commissioner of Heyang and Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he was made military commissioner of Heyang and Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 太祖登極，加同平章事，尋移鎮滄州。

translations.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, Hui was made Associate Grand Councilor and soon transferred to garrison Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he was made Associate Grand Councilor and soon reassigned to Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，就加兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was additionally made Vice Grand Secretary on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 1 he was also made Vice Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，以世宗誕慶節來朝，改邠州節度使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year he came to court for Shizong's birthday celebration and was changed to military commissioner of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he came to court for Shizong's birthday and was reassigned to Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，移鎮鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to garrison Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was moved to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 優詔贈中書令。

translations.literal: A gracious edict posthumously made him Chief Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict posthumously honored him as Chief Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 暉之儀貌不及於常人，而位極將相，年登耳順，袁、許之術，夫何恃哉！

translations.literal: Hui's bearing and appearance did not surpass ordinary men, yet he rose to the summit of general and minister, and lived to the age of sixty—of what use are the arts of Yuan and Xu!
translations.idiomatic: Hui was no better looking than the next man, yet he rose to the highest civil and military ranks and lived to sixty—what need had he of physiognomy?

sentences.zh: 然性貪鄙，而好小惠以邀虛譽，故在河陽及滄州日，民皆詣闕請立碑以頌其美，識者亦未之許也。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was greedy and base, and he liked petty favors to win empty praise; therefore during his days at Heyang and Cang Prefecture the people all went to court to request that steles be erected praising his virtues, though the discerning did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was grasping and mean, and bought cheap goodwill with small favors; while he held Heyang and Cang the people even petitioned the throne for commemorative steles—though men of judgment were not fooled.

sentences.zh: 李建崇，潞州人。

translations.literal: Li Jianchong was a native of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianchong was from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從軍，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he joined the army and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the army young and proved adept at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初事唐武皇，為鐵林都將，轉突騎、飛騎二軍使。

translations.literal: He first served Martial Emperor Wu of Tang as a general of the Iron Forest guard, then became commissioner of the Shock Cavalry and Flying Cavalry armies.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Li Keyong as a general of the Iron Forest guard, then commanded the Shock Cavalry and Flying Cavalry armies.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗攻常山，阿保機來援，莊宗率親軍千騎，遇於滿城，兵少，為契丹所圍。

translations.literal: Following Zhuangzong in the attack on Changshan, when Abaoji came to the rescue Zhuangzong led a thousand horsemen of the personal guard and met the enemy at Mancheng; his force was few and he was surrounded by the Khitans.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong attacked Changshan and Abaoji marched to relieve it, Zhuangzong led a thousand household troops to Mancheng; outnumbered, they were surrounded by the Khitans.

sentences.zh: 時建崇為親將，與契丹格鬥，自午至申，會李嗣昭騎至，契丹乃解去。

translations.literal: At that time Jianchong was a personal commander and fought the Khitans hand to hand from noon to the shen hour; when Li Sizhao's cavalry arrived, the Khitans then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchong, then a household commander, fought the Khitans from midday into the afternoon until Li Sizhao's cavalry arrived and the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 同光中，自龍武捧聖都指揮使，出歷襄、秦、徐、雍都指揮使。

translations.literal: During Tongguang he rose from Grand Commandant of the Dragon Martial Sacred Support Army to serve outside the capital in succession as Grand Commandant at Xiang, Qin, Xu, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tongguang he advanced from command of the Dragon Martial Sacred Support Army to successive grand commands at Xiang, Qin, Xu, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 建崇性純厚，處身任遇，不能巧宦，以致久滯偏裨。

translations.literal: Jianchong's nature was simple and sincere; in his conduct he accepted whatever appointment came, could not practice clever courtiership, and therefore long remained stuck among junior officers.
translations.idiomatic: Simple and honest by nature, he took whatever post he was given and never learned court craft, so he long remained a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘗掌牙兵，與建崇共事，及即位，甚湣之，連授磁、沁二郡。

translations.literal: Mingzong had once commanded the guard troops and worked with Jianchong; when he took the throne he pitied him greatly and in succession appointed him to the two prefectures of Ci and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had once commanded the guard alongside him; on taking the throne he pitied Jianchong and gave him Ci and Qin prefectures in turn.

sentences.zh: 入晉為申州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Jin he entered service as prefect of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Jin he became prefect of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天福七年冬，襄州安從進構逆，率眾寇南陽，時建崇領步騎千餘屯於葉縣，開封尹鄭王遣宣徽使張從恩、皇城使焦繼勛率在京諸軍，會建崇軍拒賊，至湖陽縣之花山，遇從進軍，建崇接戰，大敗之，以功授亳州團練使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year of Tianfu, An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture plotted rebellion and led troops to raid Nanyang; at that time Jianchong commanded more than a thousand infantry and cavalry stationed at Ye County; the Prince of Zheng, acting prefect of Kaifeng, sent Palace Secretariat Commissioner Zhang Congen and Imperial City Commissioner Jiao Jixun to lead all armies in the capital, joining Jianchong's force to resist the rebels; reaching Flower Mountain in Huyang County they met Congjin's army, Jianchong engaged and routed them, and for his merit was made regimental commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tianfu 7, when An Congjin of Xiangzhou rebelled and marched on Nanyang, Jianchong held Ye County with a thousand-odd troops; the Prince of Zheng sent Zhang Congen and Jiao Jixun with the capital armies to join him. At Flower Mountain in Huyang County Jianchong met the rebels and crushed them, earning appointment as regimental commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 襄陽平，遷安州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Xiangyang was pacified, he was transferred to defense commissioner of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangyang fell he was made defense commissioner of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷河陽、邢州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: He served in succession as military regent of Heyang and Xing Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as military regent of Heyang and Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢初，入為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he entered service as Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han he returned to court as Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 年逾七十，神氣不衰。

translations.literal: Past seventy years of age, his spirit and vigor did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, his vigor had not faded.

sentences.zh: 建崇始自代北事武皇，至是四十餘年，前後所掌兵，麾下部曲多至節鉞，零落殆盡，惟建崇雖位不及藩屏，而康強自適，以至期耄。

translations.literal: Jianchong had first served the Martial Emperor from north of Dai; by then it was more than forty years; of the troops he had commanded before and after, many subordinates under his banner had risen to military commissioner, and nearly all had perished—only Jianchong, though his rank never reached a frontier commission, remained hale and at ease until the full term of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchong had followed Li Keyong from the north forty years earlier; of the men who had served under his command, many had become military commissioners and nearly all were gone—yet he, though never made a frontier commissioner, stayed hale into his eighties.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，授左監門衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the Taizu took the throne, Jianchong was appointed Senior General of the Left Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he was made Senior General of the Left Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年春卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Guangshun he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of Guangshun 3.

sentences.zh: 贈黔南節度使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made military commissioner of Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as military commissioner of Qiannan.

sentences.zh: 王重裔，陳州宛丘人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongyi was a native of Wanqiu in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongyi was from Wanqiu in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父達，歷安、均、洺三州刺史，因家於洺。

translations.literal: His father Da served in succession as prefect of An, Jun, and Ming Prefectures, and the family settled at Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da had been prefect of An, Jun, and Ming in turn, and the family made its home at Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 重裔幼沈厚有勇，善騎射。

translations.literal: Zhongyi in youth was deep, steady, and brave, and skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi was grave and brave from boyhood and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 年未及冠，事莊宗為廳直，管契丹直。

translations.literal: Before he reached the capping age he served Zhuangzong as a hall attendant and managed Khitan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he entered Zhuangzong's service as a hall attendant in charge of Khitan affairs.

sentences.zh: 從安汴、洛，累為禁軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Bian and Luo and rose through successive posts as commandant of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Bianjing and Luoyang and rose through command posts in the palace armies.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，鎮州安重榮謀叛，稱兵指闕，朝廷命杜重威率師拒之，賊陣於宗城東，晉遣齊軍擊之，再合不動。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, An Chongrong of Zhen Prefecture plotted rebellion and raised troops toward the capital; the court ordered Du Chongwei to lead an army to resist. The rebels formed battle lines east of Zongcheng; Jin sent its army to attack, but after two engagements it did not budge.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin Tianfu, An Chongrong of Zhenzhou rebelled and marched on the capital; the court sent Du Chongwei against him. The rebels drew up east of Zongcheng; Jin forces attacked twice without shifting them.

sentences.zh: 杜重威懼，謀欲抽退，重裔曰：「兵家忌退，但請公分麾下兵擊其兩翼，重裔為公陷陣，當其中軍，彼必狼狽矣。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei grew afraid and planned to withdraw. Zhongyi said, "Warfare forbids retreat—only ask the Duke to divide his forces and strike both wings; Zhongyi will break the line for you and take the center army—they will surely fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei panicked and considered pulling back. Zhongyi said, "Armies must never retreat—split your force and hit both flanks while I break their center; they'll collapse in disarray."

sentences.zh: 」重威從之，重榮即時退蹙，遂敗。

translations.literal: Chongwei followed this; Chongrong at once drew back in distress and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei agreed; Chongrong immediately buckled and was routed.

sentences.zh: 以功遷護聖右廂都指揮使，領費州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Right Wing Grand Commandant of the Sacred Guard and given charge of Fei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made Right Wing Grand Commandant of the Sacred Guard and prefect of Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢初，仍典禁軍，從征鄴都平，遷深州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he still commanded the palace guard, followed the campaign to pacify Yedu, and was transferred to Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han he still commanded the palace armies, joined the pacification of Yedu, and was made prefect of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮夷以李守貞故，數侵邊地，以重裔為亳州防禦使，又令於徐州巡檢，兼知軍州，就加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Because of Li Shouzhen the Huai tribes repeatedly raided the borders; Zhongyi was made defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture and also ordered to inspect Xuzhou, concurrently administering the prefecture, and at once promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Huai raiders, emboldened by Li Shouzhen, harried the frontier; Zhongyi was made defense commissioner of Bozhou, assigned to inspect Xuzhou while governing the prefecture, and promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，加爵邑，改功臣。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, his noble rank and fief were increased and his merit title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu acceded, his rank and fief were raised and his merit title revised.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年夏，以疾卒，年五十有三。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Guangshun he died of illness, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the summer of Guangshun 1, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈武信軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as military commissioner of the Wuxin army.

sentences.zh: 孫漢英，太原人也。

translations.literal: Sun Hanyin was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hanyin was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父重進，事唐武皇、莊宗為大將，賜姓，名存進，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Chongjin served Martial Emperor Wu and Zhuangzong of Tang as a great general, was granted the imperial surname, and was named Cunjin; the Book of Tang has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongjin was a senior general under Li Keyong and Zhuangzong, received the imperial surname, and took the name Cunjin; the Tang History records his career.

sentences.zh: 漢英少事戎伍，稍至都將，嘗為東面馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Hanyin in youth entered the army, gradually rose to commandant, and once served as Grand Commandant of the Eastern Horse and Foot Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyin entered the ranks young, rose to commandant, and once commanded the Eastern Horse and Foot armies.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，興元節度使張虔釗失律於岐下，遂以其地西臣於蜀，漢英兄漢韶，時為洋州節度使，因茲阻隔，亦送款於蜀，由是漢英與弟漢筠久之不調。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, military commissioner of Xingyuan Zhang Qianzhao lost discipline below Qi and then with his territory submitted to Shu in the west; Hanyin's elder brother Hanshao, then military commissioner of Yang Prefecture, was cut off by this and also sent allegiance to Shu—hence Hanyin and his younger brother Hanjun long went without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai, Zhang Qianzhao of Xingyuan was defeated near Qi and surrendered his territory to Shu; Hanyin's brother Hanshao, then commissioner at Yangzhou, was stranded and submitted as well, so Hanyin and his brother Hanjun languished without posts for years.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，太祖西征蒲、雍，以漢英戚裏之分，奏於軍中指使。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era of Han, when Taizu campaigned west against Pu and Yong, because Hanyin was a relative by marriage he was recommended to command in the army.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Han Qianyou, when Taizu marched west against Pu and Yong, Hanyin—his kin by marriage—was recommended for a field command.

sentences.zh: 蒲、雍平，班師，隱帝以漢英為絳州刺史、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Pu and Yong were pacified and the army returned, the Hidden Emperor made Hanyin prefect of Jiang Prefecture and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Pu and Yong fell and the army withdrew, Emperor Yin made him prefect of Jiangzhou and Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年冬，卒於都。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Guangshun he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital in the winter of Guangshun 1.

sentences.zh: 許遷，鄆州人也。

translations.literal: Xu Qian was a native of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為本州牙將，性剛褊。

translations.literal: He first served as a military aide of his home prefecture and was by nature stern and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a military aide in his home prefecture and was stern and unyielding by nature.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，為左屯衛將軍，與少府監馬從斌同監造漢祖山陵法物，節財省用，減數萬計。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou of Han he was General of the Left Garrison Guard and, with Director of the Palace Workshops Ma Congbin, jointly supervised the ritual objects for the Han Founder's mausoleum, economizing funds and saving tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Han Qianyou he was General of the Left Garrison Guard and, with Ma Congbin of the Palace Workshops, oversaw ritual furnishings for the founding emperor's tomb, cutting costs by tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 改左監門大將軍，又加檢校司空。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grand General of the Left Gate Guard and further given the acting rank of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General of the Left Gate Guard and promoted to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 漢末，權知隰州。

translations.literal: At the end of Han he was acting administrator of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Later Han he was acting prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，劉崇遣子鈞率兵寇平陽，路由於隰，賊眾攻城，城中兵少，遷感激指諭，士鬥兼倍，賊眾傷夷，尋自退去。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Liu Chong sent his son Jun to lead troops against Pingyang; their route passed Xi, and the rebels besieged the city. Troops inside were few, but Qian, moved to inspire them, directed and exhorted—the soldiers fought at double strength, the enemy force suffered casualties, and soon withdrew on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu acceded, Liu Chong's son Jun marched on Pingyang by way of Xi. Qian rallied the outnumbered garrison; the men fought twice as hard, the besiegers took heavy losses, and soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太祖降詔撫諭，正授隰州刺史。

translations.literal: Taizu issued an edict to comfort and commend him and formally appointed him prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu issued a commendatory edict and confirmed him as prefect of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷切於除盜，嫉惡過當，或釘磔賊人，令部下臠割。

translations.literal: Qian was zealous in eliminating bandits and hated evil to excess; sometimes he nailed and dismembered bandits and had his subordinates carve their flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was relentless against bandits and punished beyond measure—sometimes nailing robbers to posts and having his men hack them apart.

sentences.zh: 誤斷不合死罪人，其家詣闕致訟，詔下開封府獄。

translations.literal: He wrongly condemned to death a man who did not deserve it; the family went to court to sue, and an edict sent the case to the Kaifeng prefectural prison.
translations.idiomatic: He once executed a man who should not have died; the family appealed to court and the case was referred to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時陳觀為知府，素與遷不協，深劾其事，欲追遷對訟，太祖以事狀可原，但罷郡而已。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Guan was prefect and had long been at odds with Qian; he impeached the matter deeply and wished to summon Qian to answer the suit. Taizu held the circumstances forgivable and only removed him from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guan, the Kaifeng prefect and Qian's longtime rival, pressed the case and sought to haul him back for trial; Taizu found the offense pardonable and merely stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 遷既奉朝請，因大詬陳觀，謂王峻曰：「相公執政，所與參議，宜求賢德。

translations.literal: Once Qian was attending court audiences, he thereupon reviled Chen Guan at length and said to Wang Jun, "When the Chancellor holds power, those with whom he consults in council ought to be sought for virtue and talent."
translations.idiomatic: As a court attendant Qian publicly denounced Chen Guan and told Wang Jun, "A chancellor ought to take counsel from men of talent and integrity."

sentences.zh: 如陳觀者，為儒無家行，為官多任情，茍知其微，屠沽兒恥與為侶，況明公乎！

translations.literal: A man like Chen Guan, as a scholar lacks household conduct, and as an official often follows whim—if one knew his true nature, even butchers and wine-sellers would be ashamed to keep his company, how much more so for Your Excellency!"
translations.idiomatic: "Men like Chen Guan disgrace the scholar's calling and govern by caprice—if his true character were known, butchers and tavern keepers would refuse his company, let alone a man of your stature!"

sentences.zh: 」峻無以沮之。

translations.literal: Jun had no way to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun could not silence him.

sentences.zh: 既而嬰疾，請告歸汶上而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill, asked leave to return to Wenshang, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill, took leave to return to Wenshang, and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳，冀州棗強縣人，幼讀書，舉童子。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng was a native of Zaoqiang County in Ji Prefecture; in youth he studied books and passed the child prodigy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng was from Zaoqiang in Jizhou; as a boy he studied and passed the child-prodigy examination.

sentences.zh: 既長，兇豪多力，以殺人暴掠為事，吏不能禁。

translations.literal: When grown he was fierce, overbearing, and strong, making killing and violent plunder his occupation; officials could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was brutal and powerful, devoted to murder and robbery; the authorities could not check him.

sentences.zh: 安重榮鎮常山，招集叛亡，鳳乃應募，既而犯法當死，即破械逾獄，遁而獲免。

translations.literal: An Chongrong held Changshan and gathered fugitive rebels; Feng then answered the call, but afterward violated the law and deserved death—he broke his shackles, crossed the prison wall, fled, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chongrong held Changshan and recruited fugitives, Feng joined him; later condemned to death, he broke his chains, scaled the prison wall, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 天福中，趙延壽為契丹鄉導，歲侵深、冀，鳳往依焉。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era Zhao Yanshou served as native guide for the Khitans, who year by year invaded Shen and Ji; Feng went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, Zhao Yanshou guided Khitan raids yearly into Shen and Jizhou; Feng threw in his lot with him.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·荊罕儒傳》：罕儒少無賴，與趙鳳、張輦為群盜，晉天福中，相率詣范陽，委贄燕王趙延壽，得掌兵權。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Jing Hanru in the Song History: Hanru in youth was a wastrel; with Zhao Feng and Zhang Zheng he formed a band of robbers. In the Tianfu era of Jin they went together to Fanyang, presented tribute to Prince of Yan Zhao Yanshou, and obtained command of troops.)
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Jing Hanru: In youth Hanru was a wastrel who, with Zhao Feng and Zhang Zheng, led a band of robbers; during Jin Tianfu they all went to Fanyang, submitted to Prince of Yan Zhao Yanshou, and won military command.)

sentences.zh: 契丹主素聞其桀黠，署為羽林軍使，累遷羽林都指揮使，常令將兵在邊，貝、冀之民，日罹其患。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler had long heard of his fierceness and cunning and appointed him commissioner of the Forest of Feathers Army; he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commandant of the Forest of Feathers and was often ordered to lead troops on the frontier—the people of Bei and Ji daily suffered his harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor, knowing his ruthlessness, made him commissioner of the Forest of Feathers guard and later its grand commandant, often posting him on the frontier; the people of Bei and Jizhou suffered under him daily.

sentences.zh: 晉末，契丹入洛，鳳從至東京，授宿州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin the Khitans entered Luoyang; Feng followed to the Eastern Capital and was made defense commissioner of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jin the Khitans took Luoyang; Feng followed them to the Eastern Capital and was made defense commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢祖即位，受代歸闕，尋授河陽行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the Han Founder took the throne, Feng was relieved and returned to court, and soon was made campaigning marshal of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han founder acceded, Feng was recalled to court and soon made campaigning marshal of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，入為龍武將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he entered service as General of the Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he returned to court as a Dragon Martial general.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起復授右千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He mourned his father's death, was recalled from mourning, and appointed Grand General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he was recalled from mourning and made Grand General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢末，都城變起，兵集之夜，無不剽之室，唯鳳里閭，兵不敢犯，人皆服其膽勇。

translations.literal: At the end of Han turmoil arose in the capital; on the night troops gathered there was no house not looted—only Feng's neighborhood did soldiers dare not violate, and all admired his daring and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Later Han, when mutiny convulsed the capital, every household was looted except Feng's lane—troops would not touch it—and all marveled at his nerve.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，用為宋、亳、宿三州巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was employed as inspector of Song, Bo, and Su Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was made inspector of Song, Bo, and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳出於伏莽，尤知盜之隱伏，乃誘致盜魁於麾下，厚待之，每桴鼓之發，無不擒捕，眾以為能，然平民因捕盜而破家者多矣。

translations.literal: Feng came from the outlaw hills and especially knew where bandits lay hidden; he therefore lured bandit chiefs under his banner and treated them generously. Whenever the drum was beaten for a raid, none failed to be seized—the crowd deemed him capable, yet many common people were ruined in the course of catching bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A brigand himself, Feng knew every hideout; he coaxed bandit leaders into his service and rewarded them well. Every raid he launched ended in captures, and he was praised for it—but countless innocents were ruined in the process.

sentences.zh: 鳳善事人，或使臣經由，靡不傾財厚奉，故得延譽而掩其醜跡。

translations.literal: Feng was skilled at courting people; whenever envoys passed through, none failed to pour out wealth in lavish gifts—thus he won extended praise and covered his ugly tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Feng cultivated officials lavishly; no envoy passed through without rich gifts, and his reputation at court masked his crimes.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其幹事，用為單州刺史，既剛忿不仁，得位逾熾，刑獄之間，尤為不道。

translations.literal: Taizu heard of his effectiveness and employed him as prefect of Shan Prefecture. Once in office he was harsh, resentful, and unkind, and with position his excess burned hotter—in judicial punishment he was especially inhumane.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, impressed by his energy, made him prefect of Shanzhou; in office he grew harsher and more cruel, and his courts became notorious for injustice.

sentences.zh: 嘗抑奪人之妻女，又以進奉南郊為名，率斂部民財貨，為人所訟。

translations.literal: He once seized other men's wives and daughters, and under the pretext of tribute for the Southern Suburban Sacrifice he led in extorting the wealth of the people of his prefecture—he was sued by others.
translations.idiomatic: He seized men's wives and daughters and, claiming tribute for the suburban sacrifice, extorted his subjects until they brought suit.

sentences.zh: 廣順三年十二月，詔削奪鳳在身官爵，尋令賜死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Guangshun an edict stripped Feng of his active offices and ranks, and soon he was ordered to take poison and die.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Guangshun 3 an edict stripped him of rank and office, and soon he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 齊藏珍，少歷內職，累遷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: Qi Cangzhen in youth passed through inner palace service and rose through successive posts as general of the guard armies.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Cangzhen began in palace service and rose through the guard armies.

sentences.zh: 前後監押兵師在外，頗稱幹事，然險诐無行，殘忍辯給，無不畏其利口。

translations.literal: Before and after he supervised and escorted armies in the field he was quite praised for effectiveness, yet he was treacherous and without conduct, cruel and glib in debate—none did not fear his sharp tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising armies in the field he won praise for efficiency, but he was treacherous, cruel, and glib—everyone feared his tongue.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，奉命滑州界巡護河堤，以弛慢致河決，除名，配沙門島。

translations.literal: In Guangshun he was ordered to patrol and guard the river dikes on the border of Hua Prefecture; through laxness a breach occurred, his name was struck from the rolls, and he was banished to Shamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun he was assigned to guard dikes near Huazhou; negligence caused a breach, he was struck from the rolls, and exiled to Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 世宗在西班時，與藏珍同列，每聆其談論，或剖判世務，似有可采。

translations.literal: When Shizong was in the western class of attendants he stood in the same rank as Cangzhen; whenever he heard his discourse, sometimes dissecting and judging affairs of the age, it seemed there was something worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong served in the western bureau he sat with Cangzhen and often found his talk on state affairs sharp enough to heed.

sentences.zh: 及即位，自流所征還。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Cangzhen was summoned back from exile.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Shizong recalled him from exile.

sentences.zh: 秦、鳳之役，令監偏師。

translations.literal: In the Qin-Feng campaign he was ordered to supervise a detached division.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qin-Feng campaign he was assigned to supervise a detached force.

sentences.zh: 及淮上用兵，復委監護，與軍校何超領兵降下光州。

translations.literal: When troops were used on the Huai he was again entrusted with supervision; with military officer He Chao he led troops to bring down Guang Prefecture in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When war resumed on the Huai he was again placed in charge and, with the officer He Chao, took Guangzhou by surrender.

sentences.zh: 藏珍欺隱官物甚多，超以為不可，藏珍曰：「沙門島已有屋數間，不妨再去矣。

translations.literal: Cangzhen concealed and embezzled many government goods; Chao held this unacceptable. Cangzhen said, "On Shamen Island I already have several rooms—going again would be no hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhen embezzled heavily; He Chao objected. Cangzhen said, "I already have a few rooms on Shamen Island—another stint there would be fine."

sentences.zh: 」其不畏法也如此。

translations.literal: Such was his fearlessness of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his contempt for the law.

sentences.zh: 世宗既破紫金山寨，追吳寇室渦口，因與藏珍言及克捷之狀。

translations.literal: After Shizong had broken the Zijin Mountain stockade and pursued Wu bandits to the mouth of Shiwu, he spoke with Cangzhen about the shape of the victory.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong stormed the Zijin Mountain camp and drove Wu forces to Shiwukou, he discussed the victory with Cangzhen.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下神武之功，近代無比，於文德則未光。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your Majesty's divine martial achievement in recent times has no equal, yet in civil virtue it is not yet radiant."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your martial prowess is unmatched in our age, but your civil accomplishments still lack luster."

sentences.zh: 」世宗頷之，又問以揚州之事，對曰：「揚州地實卑濕，食物例多腥腐。

translations.literal: Shizong nodded, then asked about Yang Prefecture. He replied, "The land of Yang Prefecture is truly low and damp; food there is mostly rank and spoiled."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong nodded, then asked about Yangzhou. He said, "Yangzhou is low and damp; the food there is mostly foul and rotten."

sentences.zh: 臣去歲在彼，人以鱔魚饋臣者，視其盤中虬屈，一如蛇虺之狀，假使鸛雀有知，亦應不食，豈況於人哉！

translations.literal: Last year when I was there someone presented eel to me; looking at the dish they coiled and twisted like the form of serpents and vipers—even if storks and magpies had understanding they would refuse to eat, how much more so for men!"
translations.idiomatic: "Last year someone served me eel there—it lay coiled in the dish like snakes. If storks and magpies had sense they would refuse it; what man could stomach it?"

sentences.zh: 」其敷奏大率多此類，聞者無不悚然。

translations.literal: His memorials to the throne were mostly of this kind; hearers were without exception startled.
translations.idiomatic: His court speeches were mostly of this sort, and all who heard them shuddered.

sentences.zh: 一日，又奏云：「唐景思已為刺史，臣猶未蒙聖澤。

translations.literal: One day he again memorialized, saying, "Tang Jingsi has already been made prefect, yet your servant has still not received imperial grace."
translations.idiomatic: One day he said, "Tang Jingsi already has a prefecture, but I have yet to receive Your Majesty's favor."

sentences.zh: 」世宗俯而從之，時濠梁未下，即命為濠州行州刺史。

translations.literal: Shizong bowed his head and assented; at the time Haoliang had not yet fallen, and he was at once made acting prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong agreed; Haoliang had not yet fallen, and he was immediately made acting prefect of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 及張永德與李重進有間言，藏珍嘗遊說重進，洎壽陽兵回，諸將中有以藏珍之言上奏者。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yongde and Li Chongjin had estranged words, Cangzhen had once gone to persuade Chongjin; when the Shouyang army returned, among the generals some reported Cangzhen's words to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yongde and Li Chongjin fell out, Cangzhen had urged Chongjin on; after the army returned from Shouyang, a general reported his words to the throne.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒，急召赴闕。

translations.literal: Shizong was angry and urgently summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong flew into a rage and summoned him to court at once.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，以其冒稱檢校官罪，按其事而斃之，蓋不欲暴其惡跡也。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, on the charge of falsely claiming an acting official rank, his case was investigated and he was executed—likely because they did not wish to expose his wicked tracks.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of his fourth year he was tried for falsely claiming an acting rank and executed—perhaps to avoid airing his full record of crimes.

sentences.zh: 王環，本真定人。

translations.literal: Wang Huan was originally a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan was originally from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 唐天成初，孟知祥鎮西川，環往事之，及知祥建號，環累典軍衛，孟昶嗣位，環兼領左、右衛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng of Tang, Meng Zhixiang held West River Circuit and Huan went to serve him; when Zhixiang established his title, Huan repeatedly directed the army guards. When Meng Chang succeeded, Huan concurrently held the Left and Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, when Meng Zhixiang governed Sichuan, Huan entered his service; after Meng declared himself ruler, Huan rose through the palace guards, and under Meng Chang he commanded both Left and Right guards.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年秋，王師西伐，時環為鳳州節度使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Xiande the imperial army campaigned west; at the time Huan was military commissioner of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Xiande 2 the Zhou army marched west; Huan was then military commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，偏師傅其城下，為環所敗，裨將胡立為環所擒。

translations.literal: At first a detached division reached below his walls and was defeated by Huan; deputy general Hu Li was captured by Huan.
translations.idiomatic: At first a detached force came to his walls and was beaten; Huan captured the deputy commander Hu Li.

sentences.zh: 是冬，王師大集，急攻其城，蜀之援兵相次敗走。

translations.literal: That winter the imperial army gathered in force and pressed the attack on his city; Shu's relief troops were in succession defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the main army assembled and assaulted the city; Shu relief columns were beaten back one after another.

sentences.zh: 環聞之，守備愈堅，王師攻擊數月方克。

translations.literal: When Huan heard this, his defense grew firmer still; the imperial army attacked for months before taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan tightened the defense; the Zhou army besieged it for months before it fell.

sentences.zh: 城陷，環就擒。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Huan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 及到闕，世宗以忠於所事，釋其罪，授若驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When he reached court, Shizong because of his loyalty to the lord he had served released his crime and appointed him Grand General of the Ruoxiao Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Brought to court, he was pardoned for his loyalty to Shu and made Grand General of the Ruoxiao Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，世宗南征，環隨駕至泗州，遇疾而卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Shizong campaigned south; Huan followed the imperial progress to Si Prefecture, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of his fourth year Shizong marched south; Huan accompanied him to Sizhou, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 張彥超，本沙陀部人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanchao was originally of the Shatuo tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanchao was originally a Shatuo tribesman.

sentences.zh: 素有郤克之疾，時號為「跛子」。

translations.literal: He had long suffered a Xi Ke-like ailment and was at the time nicknamed "the Lame One."
translations.idiomatic: He had long been lame—like Xi Ke of old—and was known as "the Lame One."

sentences.zh: 初，以騎射事唐莊宗為馬直軍使，莊宗入汴，授神武指揮使。

translations.literal: At first, through mounted archery he served Zhuangzong of Tang as commissioner of the Horse Straight Army; when Zhuangzong entered Bian, he was appointed Commandant of the Divine Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered Zhuangzong's service as a mounted archer and commissioner of the Horse Straight Army; when Zhuangzong took Bianjing, he was made commandant of the Divine Martial guard.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘗以為養子。

translations.literal: Mingzong once took him as an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong once adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 天成中，擢授蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he was promoted and appointed prefect of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was promoted to prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 素與晉高祖不協，屬其總戎於太原，遂舉其城投於契丹，即以為雲州節度使。

translations.literal: He had long been at odds with Gaozu of Jin; when the latter commanded troops at Taiyuan, Yanchao raised his city and surrendered to the Khitans, who at once made him military commissioner of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had long feuded with Shi Jingtang; when Jingtang commanded at Taiyuan, Yanchao surrendered his city to the Khitans and was made military commissioner of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹之南侵也，彥超率部眾，頗為鎮、魏之患。

translations.literal: When the Khitans invaded south, Yanchao led his tribesmen and was quite a scourge to Zhen and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On Khitan southern raids he led his followers and plagued Zhenzhou and Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 及契丹入汴，遷侍衛馬軍都校，尋授晉昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, he was transferred to colonel of the Palace Mounted Army, and soon made military commissioner of the Jinchang army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans took Bianjing he became colonel of the palace mounted guard, then military commissioner of the Jinchang army.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入洛，彥超飛表輸誠，移授保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Han entered Luoyang, Yanchao sent a swift memorial pledging loyalty and was reassigned as military commissioner of the Baoda army.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Han Gaozu entered Luoyang, Yanchao hurried a pledge of loyalty and was transferred to military commissioner of the Baoda army.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，奉詔歸闕，止奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: Early in Qianyou he returned to court by edict and held only court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he was recalled to court and held only a court-attendance post.

sentences.zh: 太祖自鄴入平內難，隱帝令彥超董騎軍為拒，劉子陂兵亂，彥超先謁見太祖。

translations.literal: When Taizu came from Ye to quell the inner turmoil, the Hidden Emperor ordered Yanchao to direct the cavalry in resistance; at the Liu zipo army disturbance Yanchao was first to pay court to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched from Ye to settle the succession crisis, Emperor Yin ordered Yanchao to command the cavalry against him; at the rout at Liu zipo, Yanchao was first to submit to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，授神武統軍。

translations.literal: During Guangshun he was appointed commander of the Divine Martial army.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun he was made commander of the Divine Martial army.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年冬，以疾終於第。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande he died of illness at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at home in the winter of Xiande 3.

sentences.zh: 制贈太子太師。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 張穎，太原人，駙馬都尉永德

translations.literal: Zhang Ying of Taiyuan, [son of] Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Yongde
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying of Taiyuan, son of Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Zhang Yongde

sentences.zh: （《宋史》列傳：永德，并州陽曲人。

translations.literal: (From the biographies in the Song History: Yongde was a native of Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, biographies: Yongde was from Yangqu in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 家世饒財，曾祖丕，尚氣節。

translations.literal: His family for generations was wealthy; his great-grandfather Pi esteemed integrity and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy for generations; his great-grandfather Pi was a man of principle.

sentences.zh: 後唐武皇鎮太原，急於用度，多嚴選富家子掌帑庫，或調度不給，即坐誅，沒入資產。

translations.literal: When Martial Emperor Wu of Later Tang held Taiyuan, urgent for funds, he often strictly selected sons of rich houses to manage the treasuries; if supplies fell short they were immediately punished by death and their assets confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong governed Taiyuan and needed money, he appointed rich men's sons to run the treasury; if they failed to meet demand they were executed and their property seized.

sentences.zh: 丕為之滿歲，府財有餘。

translations.literal: Pi held the post a full year and the prefectural treasury had a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Pi served a full year and left the prefectural treasury in surplus.

sentences.zh: 宗人政當次補其任，率族屬泣拜，請丕濟其急，丕又為代掌一年，鄉里服其義。）〉

translations.literal: Clansman Zheng was next to fill the post; he led kinsmen weeping and bowing, begging Pi to relieve his distress, and Pi again held it for them a year—the countryside honored his righteousness.)
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Zheng was due to take the post next; his kin wept and begged Pi to spare him, and Pi held it another year—the neighborhood admired his decency.)

sentences.zh: 之父也。

translations.literal: was his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde was his father.

sentences.zh: 累為藩郡列校，由內職歷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as a ranked officer in frontier prefectures and, from inner palace posts, passed through successive generals of the guard armies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through frontier garrisons and palace service to generalships in the guard armies.

sentences.zh: 國初，以戚裏之故，自華州行軍司馬歷郢、懷二州刺史，遷安州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, because of marital kin, he rose from campaigning marshal of Hua Prefecture through prefect of Ying and Huai to defense commissioner of An.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, as an imperial in-law, he rose from campaigning marshal at Huazhou to prefect of Ying and Huai, then defense commissioner of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 穎性卞急峻刻，不容人之小過，雖左右親信，亦皆怨之。

translations.literal: Ying was by nature abrupt, harsh, and severe, brooking no small fault in others—even trusted attendants all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was harsh and unforgiving; even his closest attendants resented him.

sentences.zh: 部曲曹澄有處女，穎逼而娶之，澄遂與不逞之徒數人，同謀害穎，中夜挾刃入於寢門，執穎而殺之，遂奔於金陵。

translations.literal: His retainer Cao Cheng had a virgin daughter whom Ying forced into marriage; Cheng then with several ruffians conspired to kill Ying, at midnight blades in hand entered the sleeping gate, seized Ying and slew him, then fled to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His retainer Cao Cheng had a daughter whom Ying seized in marriage; Cheng and several ruffians murdered him at midnight in his bedchamber and fled to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，以永德之故，遣江南李景，令執澄等送行在。

translations.literal: Shizong campaigning on the Huai sent to Li Jing in Jiangnan because of Yongde, ordering Cheng and the others seized and sent to the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong campaigned on the Huai, he demanded of Li Jing in Jiangnan, for Yongde's sake, that Cheng and his accomplices be seized and sent to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及至，世宗以澄等賜永德，俾甘心而戮之。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Shizong gave Cheng and the others to Yongde so he might satisfy his heart and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Shizong handed them to Yongde to kill as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 劉仁贍，略通儒術，好兵書，在澤國甚有聲望。

translations.literal: Liu Renshan had some grasp of Confucian learning, loved military treatises, and in the lake-marsh country enjoyed great repute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renshan knew some classics, loved military texts, and was highly regarded in the Yangtze delta.

sentences.zh: 吳主知之，累遷為偽右監門衛將軍，歷黃、袁二州刺史，所至稱治。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler knew him and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, and as prefect of Huang and Yuan his rule was praised wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler noticed him and made him Acting Grand General of the Right Gate Guard; as prefect of Huang and Yuan he won praise for good government.

sentences.zh: 洎李景僭襲偽位，俾掌親軍，遷鄂州節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Jing usurped the false throne, he was made to command the personal armies and transferred as military commissioner of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing seized the Southern Tang throne, he put Renshan in charge of the household armies and made him military commissioner of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 居數年，復以兵柄任之，改壽州節度使。

translations.literal: After several years he was again entrusted with military authority and made military commissioner of Shou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was again given command of troops and transferred to military commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 及王師渡淮，而仁贍固守甚堅。

translations.literal: When the imperial army crossed the Huai, Renshan defended with extreme firmness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army crossed the Huai, Renshan held Shouzhou with fierce tenacity.

sentences.zh: 洎世宗駐蹕於其壘北，數道齊攻，填塹陷壁，晝夜不息，如是者累月。

translations.literal: When Shizong halted north of his ramparts, they attacked on many routes together, filling moats and breaching walls, day and night without cease—thus for many months.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong camped north of the walls and assaulted from every side, filling moats and smashing battlements day and night for months on end.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨城以諭之，而仁贍但遜詞以謝。

translations.literal: Shizong came before the walls to admonish him, but Renshan only returned humble words of refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong came to the walls to summon him, but Renshan answered only with polite refusal.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還京，命李重進總兵守之，復乘間陷我南寨。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, Li Chongjin was ordered to command troops in siege; Renshan again seized an interval and took our southern stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Li Chongjin was left to besiege the city; Renshan seized an opening and overran the southern Zhou camp.

sentences.zh: 自是圍之愈急，城中饑死者甚眾。

translations.literal: From then the siege grew tighter and within the city many died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The siege tightened; starvation killed multitudes inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，淮寇復來救援，列寨於紫金山，夾道相屬，累然數十里，垂及壽壁，而重進兵幾不能支，世宗患之，遂復議親征。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year Huai bandits came again to relieve the siege, lining stockades on Zijin Mountain, linked along the road for dozens of li, nearly reaching the walls of Shou; Chongjin's army could barely hold, Shizong was troubled, and debated returning to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Southern Tang relief forces camped on Zijin Mountain in a chain of stockades miles long, nearly linking to Shouzhou's walls; Chongjin's army nearly broke, and Shizong resolved to take the field himself.

sentences.zh: 車駕至壽春，命今上率師破紫金山之眾，擒其應援使陳承昭以獻。

translations.literal: The carriage reached Shouchun; the present sovereign was ordered to lead troops to break the Zijin Mountain host and present the relief commissioner Chen Chengzhao captured.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouchun he ordered the future emperor—then Zhao Kuangyin—to rout the Zijin Mountain relief force and present the captured relief commissioner Chen Chengzhao.

sentences.zh: 仁贍聞援兵既敗，計無所出，但扼腕浩嘆而已。

translations.literal: Renshan heard the relief army was beaten and had no plan left—only clutched his wrist and sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the relief army was destroyed, Renshan had no recourse but to wring his hands and sigh.

sentences.zh: 會世宗以紫金山之捷，飛詔以諭之，時仁贍臥疾已亟，因翻然納款，而城內諸軍萬計，皆屏息以聽其命。

translations.literal: When Shizong with the Zijin victory sent a flying edict to summon him, Renshan was already gravely ill abed and thereupon suddenly submitted; the myriad troops in the city all held their breath and obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zijin victory Shizong sent a swift summons; Renshan, already gravely ill, at once surrendered, and the city's ten thousand defenders obeyed him in silence.

sentences.zh: 及見於行在，世宗撫之甚厚，賜與加等，復令入城養病，尋授天平軍節度使、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When he appeared at the headquarters Shizong comforted him generously, gifts above the norm, and sent him back to the city to recover; soon he was made military commissioner of Tianping and concurrent Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: At headquarters Shizong received him with great kindness and lavish gifts, sent him back to the city to convalesce, and soon appointed him military commissioner of Tianping and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 制出之日，薨於其家，年五十八。

translations.literal: On the day the appointment was issued he died at home, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The day the commission was promulgated he died at home, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，遣使吊祭，命內臣監護喪事，追封彭城郡王。

translations.literal: Shizong heard, sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, ordered inner palace officials to supervise the funeral, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent mourners, placed eunuchs in charge of the funeral, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 後以其子崇讃為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁贍輕財重士，法令嚴肅，重圍之中，其子崇諫犯軍禁，即令斬之，故能以一城之眾，連年拒守。

translations.literal: Renshan prized scholars and spent lightly on wealth, his laws stern; in the deep siege his son Chongjian violated military prohibition and was at once ordered beheaded—hence with one city's multitude he could resist for years.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan was generous to scholars and strict in law; during the siege his son Chongjian broke military discipline and was executed on the spot—which is why one city could hold out for years.

sentences.zh: 逮其來降，而其下未敢竊議者，保其後嗣，抑有由焉。

translations.literal: When he came to surrender, his subordinates dared not whisper in private—protecting his descendants, and this too had its reason.
translations.idiomatic: When he surrendered, his men dared not murmur against him—they knew he had secured their families' futures, and for good reason.

sentences.zh: 崇贊仕周，累為郡守。

translations.literal: Chongzan served Zhou and rose through successive prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzan served the Zhou and held several prefectures in succession.

sentences.zh: 幼子崇諒，後自江南歸於本朝，亦位至省郎。

translations.literal: The youngest son Chongliang later returned from Jiangnan to the dynasty and also reached a post as a ministry secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Chongliang later came home from Jiangnan and rose to a post in the central ministries.
